headline: No votes were recorded; the airport director outlined federal grants, airline costs, a planned fire station move, and new Nashville flights.
summary: The airport director gave an update on projects, finances, safety, air service, and customer programs. The update covered a $15 million federal funding request and a $303,000 grant for vehicle transponders. No votes or motions with results were recorded.
discussion: Airfield safety: The director described moving the aircraft rescue firefighting station to the west side of the airfield, and vehicle transponders that let the tower see equipment on the runway.

Airline costs: The director said a new five-year airline operating agreement is expected to be signed this fall, and debt restructuring is expected to cut airline operating costs by about $7 million a year.
Master plan update: Public meetings were held in September, and a master plan report is planned by Q2 of 2027.
Air service: Southwest began new Nashville service on October 1, and Southwest plans Fort Myers service starting in the winter months.
Drainage and runoff: Members asked about runoff into the Merrimack River from firefighting chemicals, and the director said an environmental company monitors quarterly and during de-icing events.
